mainTopic: The scope of קימה and הידור for elders and scholars: cost, place, distance, the elder's own duty, and who counts as a זקן
overview: The גמרא first finishes proving from the wording of the פסוק that שיבה and זקן describe one person. It then works through the ברייתא line by line. קימה and הידור are compared in both directions, so honoring an elder never requires stopping work or spending money. From this comes the rule that בעלי אומניות may not stand for תלמידי חכמים while they are working, and the standing shown to those bringing ביכורים is explained as a special case. Next, the גמרא splits the bathhouse into rooms: there is no standing in the inner rooms, but standing is required in the outer rooms. The גמרא also teaches that a person may not close his eyes ahead of time to escape the מצוה. It sets the distance for standing at four אמות, and for one's רב מובהק it is as far as one can see. On the elder's side, he should not trouble people, and a scholar who walks around them is promised long life. Finally, רבי יוחנן rules like איסי בן יהודה that every elderly person deserves honor, and stories show how different אמוראים honored and helped elders.

steps.title: The verse's wording shows שיבה and זקן are one person
steps.stepSummary: If the Torah meant two separate people, it would have repeated 'stand and honor' for each one. Since it did not, שיבה and זקן describe one person.
steps.simpleTranslation: If they were two, the Torah would have written: 'Before the old one you shall stand and honor; you shall stand and honor the face of the elder.' Since it did not write it that way, learn from this that it is one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes an argument from just before this point. It shows that the פסוק treats שיבה and זקן as one single person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof comes from what the פסוק does not say. Two separate groups would each have needed their own 'תקום והדרת'. The פסוק uses that phrase only once, joining שיבה and זקן together, so they are one category.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from it (a proof is established)

phrases.english: "Before the old one you shall stand and honor,
phrases.notes: This is how the פסוק would have looked if they were two people. The real פסוק is ויקרא 19:32.

phrases.english: you shall stand and honor the face of an elder."
And since [the Torah] did not write it this way,
learn from it that it is one.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִדְּלָא כְּתַב הָכִי, שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ חַד הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the discussion from the previous section about whether שיבה and זקן are two separate people
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: שיבה and זקן in the פסוק refer to one single person.

steps.title: Honoring an elder does not require spending money
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא: הידור does not mean giving money, because it is paired with קימה, which costs nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: You might think one must honor him with money. So the פסוק says 'stand and honor.' Just as standing costs no money, so too honoring is something that costs no money.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the ברייתא quoted earlier and quotes one of its lines. It is setting up a question on that line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא learns about הידור from its partner word in the פסוק, קימה. Standing up is assumed to be free, so הידור must also be the kind of honor that costs nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: Loss of money (literally, a lack in the pocket)

phrases.english: The Master said:
One might think he should honor him with money?
The verse says: "You shall stand and honor"

phrases.aramaic: מָה קִימָה שֶׁאֵין בָּהּ חֶסְרוֹן כִּיס –
phrases.english: just as standing involves no loss of money,

phrases.aramaic: אַף הִידּוּר שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ חֶסְרוֹן כִּיס.
phrases.english: so too honoring involves no loss of money.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר: יָכוֹל יְהַדְּרֶנּוּ בְּמָמוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the ברייתא to examine a new line in it
steps.mimraCoreRuling: הידור of an elder does not require spending money, learned from its pairing with קימה.

steps.title: Standing up can cost a worker money
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions the claim that קימה never costs money. A pearl-driller who stops to stand up loses valuable work time.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does standing really cost no money? What about a person drilling pearls? Meanwhile he stands up for the elder and stops his work!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the assumption behind the ברייתא, that standing is always free.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא's comparison only works if קימה never costs money. A highly paid worker loses money every moment he stops. So קימה can involve חסרון כיס, and the comparison seems to fall apart.

keyTerms.meaning: Are we not dealing with (a case where...)

phrases.english: And standing has no loss of money?

phrases.aramaic: מִי לָא עָסְקִינַן דְּקָא נָקֵיב מַרְגָּנִיתָא,
phrases.english: Are we not dealing even with someone who was drilling pearls,
and in the meantime he stands up before him
and stops his work!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְקִימָה לֵית בַּהּ חֶסְרוֹן כִּיס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the assumption behind the ברייתא in step 2
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's assumption that קימה never involves חסרון כיס
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A worker who stops to stand loses wages, so קימה can cost money. That makes it a bad model for a cost-free הידור.

steps.title: The verse compares standing and honoring in both directions
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק links קימה and הידור both ways. From הידור we learn that קימה does not require stopping work. From that limited קימה we learn that הידור does not require money.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the פסוק compared standing to honoring: just as honoring does not involve stopping work, so too standing does not involve stopping work. And it also compared honoring to standing: just as standing involves no loss of money, so too honoring involves no loss of money.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by reading the comparison in the פסוק as working in both directions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: First, קימה learns from הידור, so a worker does not have to stop working to stand. Now קימה never costs money, because it only applies when no work is lost. Then הידור learns from this limited קימה that it too never costs money, so the ברייתא's rule stands.
steps.whatToRemember: The היקש between קימה and הידור works both ways: no stopping work for קימה, and no spending money for הידור.

phrases.english: Rather: [the verse] compared standing to honoring.
Just as honoring involves no stopping of work,
so too standing involves no stopping of work.
And it also compared honoring to standing:

phrases.aramaic: מָה קִימָה שֶׁאֵין בָּהּ חֶסְרוֹן כִּיס –
phrases.english: just as standing involves no loss of money,

phrases.aramaic: אַף הִידּוּר שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ חֶסְרוֹן כִּיס.
phrases.english: so too honoring involves no loss of money.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: אַקֵּישׁ קִימָה לְהִידּוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 3
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the comparison as working in both directions
steps.terutzHavaAmina: קימה always costs nothing, so it simply teaches about הידור, and the pearl-driller case breaks this.
steps.terutzMaskana: קימה is first limited to cases with no work lost, so it really is cost-free, and it then teaches that הידור is cost-free too.

steps.title: Craftsmen may not stand for scholars while working
steps.stepSummary: From this two-way comparison the חכמים ruled that בעלי אומניות may not stand for תלמידי חכמים while they are working.
steps.simpleTranslation: From here they said: craftsmen are not permitted to stand before Torah scholars while they are busy with their work.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a practical rule from the previous step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since קימה does not apply when it means stopping work, a working craftsman should not stand up. The language is strong: he is not even permitted to stand, not just excused from standing.
steps.confusionAlert: The rule does not say 'not obligated.' It says 'not permitted.' This rule is what the next step challenges.

phrases.english: From here they said:
craftsmen are not permitted
to stand before Torah scholars
while they are busy with their work.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִכָּאן אָמְרוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Practical rule derived from the היקש in step 4
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: בעלי אומניות may not stand for תלמידי חכמים during their work.

steps.title: A משנה shows craftsmen standing up for people
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the rule from a משנה. Craftsmen stood up and greeted the people bringing ביכורים to ירושלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they don't stand? But we learned in a משנה: all the craftsmen stand before them, greet them, and say to them: 'Our brothers, people of such-and-such place, welcome!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question on the rule from step 5, using a משנה about ביכורים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, working craftsmen stop to stand for the people bringing ביכורים. If they stop work for them, it seems they should surely stand for תלמידי חכמים. So the rule that they may not stand looks wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: First fruits brought to the בית המקדש

phrases.english: And they don't?
But didn't we learn in a משנה:
all the craftsmen stand before them,
phrases.notes: "Them" means the people bringing ביכורים to ירושלים. This is משנה ביכורים 3:3.

phrases.english: and greet them,
and say to them:
Our brothers, people of such-and-such place,
welcome!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא? וְהָתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rule of step 5 from a משנה
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that בעלי אומניות may not stand for תלמידי חכמים while working
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Craftsmen stop work to stand for the people bringing ביכורים, so it seems they should surely stand for תלמידי חכמים.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: the standing was only for the people bringing ביכורים
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers that the משנה's standing applies only to the people bringing ביכורים. Craftsmen do not stand for תלמידי חכמים while working.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: Before them they stand; before Torah scholars they do not stand.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers the challenge by limiting the משנה to its own case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה describes a special case, the people bringing ביכורים, and it cannot be stretched to other people. So the rule from step 5 holds: a working craftsman does not stand for a תלמיד חכם.
steps.whatToRemember: A working craftsman does not stand for a תלמיד חכם. The standing in the משנה of ביכורים is a special case only for those bringing ביכורים.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
Before them they stand,
before Torah scholars they do not stand.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: מִפְּנֵיהֶם עוֹמְדִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 6
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the source to its specific case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since craftsmen stand for people bringing ביכורים, they should surely stand for תלמידי חכמים.
steps.terutzMaskana: The standing is limited to people bringing ביכורים. For תלמידי חכמים, working craftsmen do not stand.

steps.title: A מצוה done at its proper time is precious
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי בר אבין learns from the ביכורים case how dear a מצוה is when done at its proper time.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי בר אבין said: See how beloved a מצוה is at its proper time. Craftsmen stood up for the people bringing ביכורים, but they do not stand up for תלמידי חכמים.
steps.whatsHappening: Building on the last step, רבי יוסי בר אבין draws a lesson. Workers stopped working to stand for the people bringing ביכורים, but they do not stop for a תלמיד חכם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a תלמיד חכם gets more honor than a regular person. Here, ordinary people doing a מצוה got even more honor. רבי יוסי בר אבין says the reason is that they were doing a מצוה at its proper time.

keyTerms.meaning: A מצוה done at its proper time
Come and see. A phrase that introduces a lesson.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei bar Avin said:
Come and see how beloved
is a מצוה at its proper time,
for they stand up before them,
phrases.notes: "Them" means the people bringing ביכורים, from the משנה in step 6.

phrases.english: but before Torah scholars they do not stand.

steps.triggerLanguage: בּוֹא וּרְאֵה כַּמָּה חֲבִיבָה מִצְוָה בִּשְׁעָתָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a general lesson from רבי יוחנן's answer in step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A מצוה at its proper time is so precious that its doers get more honor than תלמידי חכמים.

steps.title: Perhaps ביכורים is a special case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back. The extra honor may be a special rule for ביכורים, so that people keep coming to bring them.
steps.simpleTranslation: But perhaps ביכורים is different. If they were not honored, you would cause them to stumble in the future.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions רבי יוסי בר אבין's lesson. It suggests the honor shown to those bringing ביכורים has a different reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If people bringing ביכורים were not warmly greeted, they might stop coming next time. So the honor may be a special step to protect the מצוה of ביכורים. It does not prove that every מצוה at its proper time outranks a תלמיד חכם.

keyTerms.meaning: But perhaps. Raises another possible reason.

phrases.english: But perhaps it is different there,
for if so,
phrases.notes: He means: if they were not given this honor.

phrases.english: you would cause them to stumble in the future.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְדִלְמָא שָׁאנֵי הָתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the general lesson of step 8 by offering a reason that applies only to ביכורים.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof that any מצוה at its proper time outranks honor for תלמידי חכמים.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ביכורים honor may be a special rule to keep people bringing ביכורים, not a sign of how precious מצוות are in general.
steps.whatToRemember: The extra honor for those bringing ביכורים may be a special rule to keep the מצוה going. It is not a general rule for all מצוות.

steps.title: Must one stand in a bathhouse? The story of רבי חייא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא's rule that one does not stand in a lavatory or bathhouse. It challenges this with a story where רבי שמעון בר רבי was upset that רבי חייא did not stand for him in a bathhouse.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: One might think he should stand for an elder in a lavatory or bathhouse. Is that really so? רבי חייא was sitting in a bathhouse, and רבי שמעון בר רבי passed by. רבי חייא did not stand, and רבי שמעון was upset. He told his father: I taught him two of the five books of תהלים, and he did not stand for me!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to an earlier ברייתא, which said one does not stand for an elder in a bathhouse. It challenges that rule with a story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא learned from the word הידור that standing applies only in a place fit for honor. That leaves out a bathhouse. But רבי שמעון בר רבי expected his student to stand for him in a bathhouse, so honor seems to apply even there.

keyTerms.meaning: Fifths. Here, sections of the book of תהלים.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבי שמעון was just being touchy. The גמרא uses his complaint to show he believed standing applies even in a bathhouse, which goes against the ברייתא.

phrases.english: The Master said:
One might think he should stand before him
in the lavatory and in the bathhouse.
phrases.notes: The ברייתא went on to say "תקום והדרת": stand only where there is honor (הידור).

phrases.english: And one does not?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא רַבִּי חִיָּיא הֲוָה יָתֵיב בֵּי מַסְחוּתָא
phrases.english: But Rabbi Chiyya was sitting in a bathhouse

phrases.aramaic: וְחָלֵיף וְאָזֵיל רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בַּר רַבִּי,
phrases.english: and Rabbi Shimon son of Rebbi passed by,
and he did not stand before him, and he was upset,
and he came and said to his father:

phrases.aramaic: שְׁנֵי חוּמָּשִׁים שָׁנִיתִי לוֹ בְּסֵפֶר תְּהִלִּים,
phrases.english: I taught him two fifths of the book of Psalms,
phrases.notes: תהלים is split into five books. He taught רבי חייא two of them.

phrases.english: and he did not stand before me!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא? וְהָא רַבִּי חִיָּיא הֲוָה יָתֵיב בֵּי מַסְחוּתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the ביכורים discussion and returns to an earlier line of the ברייתא about where standing applies.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's rule that one does not stand for an elder in a lavatory or bathhouse.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי שמעון בר רבי expected his student to stand in a bathhouse, which suggests the honor applies even there.

steps.title: A second bathhouse story with בר קפרא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא adds a similar story. This time רבי answers his son that the student may have been deep in thought about what he had learned.
steps.simpleTranslation: Also: בר קפרא (some say רבי שמואל בר רבי יוסי) was sitting in a bathhouse. רבי שמעון בר רבי came in and passed by, and he did not stand. רבי שמעון was upset and told his father: I taught him two ninths of תורת כהנים, and he did not stand for me! רבי answered: Perhaps he was sitting and thinking about them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא strengthens its challenge with a second, similar story. Here we also hear רבי's reply to his son.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Again a student did not stand in a bathhouse, and רבי שמעון was upset. רבי did not answer that a bathhouse needs no standing. He excused the student only because he may have been busy thinking about his learning.

keyTerms.meaning: The halachic midrash on ויקרא (the ספרא)
Thinking it over, deep in thought

phrases.english: And furthermore:
Bar Kappara, and some say
Rabbi Shmuel bar Rabbi Yosei,
was sitting in a bathhouse.

phrases.aramaic: עָל וְאָזֵיל רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בַּר רַבִּי
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon son of Rebbi entered and passed by
and he did not stand before him, and he was upset,
and he came and said to his father:

phrases.aramaic: שְׁנֵי שְׁלִישֵׁי שְׁלִישׁ שָׁנִיתִי לוֹ בְּתוֹרַת כֹּהֲנִים –
phrases.english: I taught him two thirds of a third of Torat Kohanim,
and he did not stand before me!
And he said to him:
phrases.notes: "He" is רבי, the father, answering his son.

phrases.english: Perhaps he was sitting and thinking about them.
phrases.notes: "Them" means the teachings his son had taught him.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתוּ: בַּר קַפָּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second story to strengthen the challenge from step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's rule that one does not stand in a bathhouse.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי excused the student only because he was thinking about his learning. He never said that standing does not apply in a bathhouse.

steps.title: Inference from רבי's answer: one must stand even in a bathhouse
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא spells out the proof. The only excuse was that the student was deep in thought, so without that excuse he would have had to stand.
steps.simpleTranslation: The reason he was excused is that he was sitting and thinking about them. Otherwise, no, he would not have been excused!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws the conclusion from רבי's answer. This finishes the challenge against the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי's excuse was about the student's thinking, not about the place. So in a bathhouse a person still must stand for a חכם, which seems to go against the ברייתא. The challenge is now fully set up, and the גמרא must answer it.

keyTerms.meaning: But if not so, no. Draws a conclusion from what was not said.

steps.whatToRemember: Both bathhouse stories suggest a person must stand for a תלמיד חכם even in a bathhouse. This is a strong challenge to the ברייתא.

phrases.english: The reason is that he was sitting and thinking about them,
but if it were not so, no!
phrases.notes: He means: without that excuse, not standing would have been wrong.

steps.triggerLanguage: טַעְמָא דְּבָהֶן יוֹשֵׁב וּמְהַרְהֵר, הָא לָאו הָכִי לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from רבי's reply in step 11 to complete the challenge.
steps.raayaObject: That one must stand for a תלמיד חכם even in a bathhouse, against the ברייתא.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי's reply that the student was only excused because he was deep in thought.

steps.title: Inner rooms versus outer rooms of the bathhouse
steps.stepSummary: The two sources are about different parts of the bathhouse. The ברייתא's exemption covers the inner rooms. The stories, where standing was expected, took place in the outer rooms.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not a contradiction. This rule (no standing) is about the inner rooms. That rule (standing is required) is about the outer rooms.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction from steps 10-12. It says each source is talking about a different room in the bathhouse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the inner rooms people are undressed, so standing there is not a real show of honor. In the outer rooms people are still dressed, so standing there is respectful and required. The stories took place in the outer rooms.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult. This signals an answer that splits the two sources into two different cases.
Inner rooms, where people are undressed.
Outer rooms, where people are still dressed.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
this is in the inner rooms,
phrases.notes: "This" is the ברייתא's rule that you don't stand in a bathhouse.

phrases.english: that is in the outer rooms.
phrases.notes: "That" is the stories, where standing was expected.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא: הָא בְּבָתֵּי גַּוָּאֵי, הָא בְּבָתֵּי בָּרָאֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction proven in step 12.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא exempts standing in any part of the bathhouse, so the stories contradict it.
steps.terutzMaskana: The exemption is only for the inner rooms. In the outer rooms, standing is required.

steps.title: Support from רבי יוחנן's rule about thinking Torah
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says thinking Torah is forbidden in a bathhouse. So רבי's excuse, that the student was thinking about his learning, only makes sense in a room where such thinking is allowed. That would be the outer rooms.
steps.simpleTranslation: This also makes sense. רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: everywhere a person may think about Torah, except in a bathhouse or a lavatory.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings support for its answer that the stories happened in the outer rooms.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 11, רבי excused the student because he may have been thinking about his learning. Thinking Torah is forbidden in the bathhouse proper. So the story must have taken place in a part of the bathhouse where that is allowed, the outer rooms. This fits the answer of step 13.

keyTerms.meaning: So too it is logical. This introduces support for the answer just given.
To think about Torah in one's mind, without saying it out loud.

phrases.english: So too it is reasonable,
as Rabba bar bar Ḥana said
that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
Everywhere one is permitted to think about Torah
except for the bathhouse and the lavatory.
phrases.notes: So if the student was thinking Torah, he must have been somewhere it's allowed. That means the outer rooms.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי נָמֵי מִסְתַּבְּרָא, דְּאָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings support for the answer in step 13.
steps.raayaObject: The answer that the stories took place in the outer rooms.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוחנן's rule that thinking Torah is forbidden in a bathhouse, together with רבי's excuse that the student was thinking about his learning.

steps.title: Maybe the student could not help it
steps.stepSummary: The support is pushed away. The student may have been so caught up in his learning that he could not stop thinking, even in a forbidden place.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps someone who is overcome by his thoughts is different.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the support from step 14.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The support assumed the student was only thinking Torah where it is allowed. But a person deeply absorbed in learning may keep thinking without meaning to, even in the inner rooms. So the story does not prove where it happened. The answer of step 13 still stands, but without this support.

keyTerms.meaning: Perhaps. This often introduces a pushback.
His being forced, meaning something out of his control.

phrases.english: Perhaps one who is overcome is different.
phrases.notes: He means the student was so deep in thought that he couldn't stop, even where thinking Torah is not allowed.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּילְמָא לְאוּנְסֵיהּ שָׁאנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the support brought in step 14.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the support from רבי יוחנן. The answer of step 13 itself is not rejected.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The support assumed the student thought Torah only where it was allowed. He may have been thinking without control.

steps.title: Would anyone close his eyes on purpose?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא: one might think a person may close his eyes as if he did not see the elder. It asks whether the ברייתא is talking about wicked people.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא says: one might think he may close his eyes as if he did not see the elder. The גמרא asks: are we dealing with wicked people?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to another line of the same ברייתא and questions it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Pretending not to see someone, just to avoid a מצוה, is a plainly wicked act. A ברייתא would not need a פסוק to forbid that. So the גמרא asks what the ברייתא really means.

keyTerms.meaning: One might think. This opens a possible mistake that the פסוק then rules out.
Is it so that...? This is a question showing surprise.

phrases.english: One might think he may close his eyes
like one who did not see him.
Are we dealing with wicked people?

steps.triggerLanguage: אַטּוּ בְּרַשִּׁיעֵי עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new line of the same ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's line about closing one's eyes as if he did not see the elder.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Openly pretending not to see someone, to avoid a מצוה, is obviously wicked. It needs no special teaching from a פסוק.

steps.title: Closing his eyes before the duty begins
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא means a smarter trick. A person closes his eyes while the elder is still far away, before he must stand, so that he never sees the elder when the duty begins. The פסוק says 'and you shall fear' to forbid even this.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, one might think he may close his eyes before the time of obligation arrives. Then, when it arrives, he does not see the elder and so does not have to stand. So the פסוק says: 'You shall stand... and you shall fear.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reinterprets the ברייתא. It is talking about a person who avoids the duty before it even starts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This person never ignores an active duty. He simply makes sure he will not see the elder when the duty arrives. That might seem permitted, but the words 'and you shall fear' teach that this trick is also forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: The time when the obligation begins. Here, when the elder comes close enough that one must stand.
You shall stand... and you shall fear (ויקרא 19:32).

steps.whatToRemember: Avoiding a מצוה by setting things up beforehand, so the duty never reaches you, is also forbidden. 'And you shall fear' teaches this.
steps.whyThisMatters: It teaches that a person may not use clever tricks to escape a מצוה before it even begins.

phrases.english: Rather: one might think he may close his eyes
before the time of obligation reaches him,
so that when the time of obligation arrives
he does not see him
so as to stand before him,
the verse teaches: "You shall stand... and you shall fear."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 19:32

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: יָכוֹל יַעֲצִים עֵינָיו מִקַּמֵּי דְּלִימְטְיֵהּ זְמַן חִיּוּבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 16 by rereading the ברייתא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא warns against openly pretending not to see the elder.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא warns against closing one's eyes before the duty begins, so as to escape it. 'And you shall fear' forbids this.

steps.title: Standing counts as honor within four אמות
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that standing is a real act of honor only within four אמות of the elder.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: What kind of standing shows honor? It is standing within four אמות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a teaching that sets the distance at which you must stand for an elder: four אמות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Standing up only shows respect when people can tell you are standing for the elder. If he is very far away, your standing does not clearly honor him. So the duty starts when he is within four אמות.

phrases.aramaic: תָּנָא: אֵיזוֹהִי קִימָה שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּהּ הִידּוּר –
phrases.english: It was taught: Which standing has honor in it?
You must say: this is within four cubits.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא: אֵיזוֹהִי קִימָה שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּהּ הִידּוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the closing-eyes question to the distance at which standing is required.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Standing for an elder is required, and counts as honor, within four אמות.

steps.title: For one's main teacher, stand as soon as you see him
steps.stepSummary: אביי limits the four אמות rule to a teacher who is not one's main teacher. For one's main teacher you stand as soon as he comes into view.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: We only said four אמות for a teacher who is not his main teacher. For his main teacher, he stands as soon as he sees him.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי adds a limit to the four אמות rule. It applies to a regular teacher, but a רב מובהק gets more honor.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The four אמות rule is the basic level of honor. A רב מובהק, the teacher you learned most of your Torah from, deserves more. So you stand the moment he is within sight, even from far away.

keyTerms.meaning: We only said this about... (limits an earlier rule)
One's main teacher, from whom he learned most of his Torah
As far as his eyes can see

steps.confusionAlert: אביי is not cancelling the four אמות rule. He is saying it covers a regular teacher, and a main teacher gets a wider range.

phrases.english: Abaye said: We said this only
about his teacher who is not his main teacher,
but for his main teacher, as far as his eyes can see.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: לָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא בְּרַבּוֹ שֶׁאֵינוֹ מוּבְהָק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the four אמות rule to a teacher who is not one's main teacher.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For a רב מובהק, one stands as soon as he is within sight.

steps.title: אביי stood when he saw his teacher's donkey
steps.stepSummary: אביי would stand as soon as he saw the ear of רב יוסף's donkey coming.
steps.simpleTranslation: When אביי saw the ear of רב יוסף's donkey coming, he would stand up.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells how אביי himself followed his rule. He stood for his main teacher, רב יוסף, the moment anything of him came into view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This shows the rule of מלא עיניו in practice. אביי did not wait until רב יוסף was close. Seeing even the donkey's ear was enough.

phrases.english: Abaye, from when he would see
the ear of Rav Yosef's donkey coming,
he would stand.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבָּיֵי מִכִּי הֲוָה חָזֵי לֵיהּ לְאוּדְנֵיהּ דְּחַמְרָא דְּרַב יוֹסֵף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows אביי's own practice that matches his rule about a main teacher.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that for a רב מובהק one stands as soon as he is seen.
steps.raayaSupportSource: אביי's behavior toward his main teacher רב יוסף.

steps.title: The rabbis across the river did not stand for אביי
steps.stepSummary: אביי rode by on the far bank of a river, and רב משרשיא and other rabbis did not stand. אביי asked them if he was not their main teacher.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי was riding a donkey along the bank of the Sagya River. רב משרשיא and other rabbis sat on the other side and did not stand. He said to them: Am I not your main teacher?
steps.whatsHappening: In this story אביי challenges his students. By his own rule, they should have stood for him as soon as he was in view, even from across the river.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The distance was much more than four אמות, but for a רב מובהק that does not matter. So אביי asks why they did not stand. The question sets up their answer in the next step.

phrases.english: Abaye was riding a donkey
and going along the bank of the Sagya River,

phrases.aramaic: יָתֵיב רַב מְשַׁרְשְׁיָא וְרַבָּנַן בְּאִידַּךְ גִּיסָא
phrases.english: Rav Mesharshiyya and the rabbis were sitting on the other side
and they did not stand before him.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לְהוּ: וְלָאו רַב מוּבְהָק אֲנָא?
phrases.english: He said to them: Am I not a main teacher?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ: וְלָאו רַב מוּבְהָק אֲנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A story that tests the מלא עיניו rule from step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: The students' failure to stand for אביי.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A רב מובהק must be honored as soon as he is seen, even from far, so they should have stood.

steps.title: The students had not noticed him
steps.stepSummary: The students answered that they had not noticed אביי at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: It was not in our minds. We did not notice you.
steps.whatsHappening: The students explain that they were not showing disrespect. They simply did not see him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule of מלא עיניו depends on actually seeing the teacher. If they never noticed him, the duty to stand never started. So the rule stays in place, and they did nothing wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: It was not on our minds; we did not notice

steps.whatToRemember: For a main teacher you stand as far as you can see him. The duty starts only once you actually see him.

phrases.english: They said to him: It was not on our minds.
phrases.notes: They mean they never noticed you, so the duty to stand never started.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ: לָאו אַדַּעְתִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge from step 21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Factual: the case did not trigger the obligation.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The students ignored a main teacher they could see.
steps.terutzMaskana: They never noticed him, so there was no duty to stand.

steps.title: An elder should not burden people with his honor
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר learns from the פסוק 'זקן ויראת' that an elder should not trouble people to stand for him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says: Where do we learn that an elder should not trouble people? The פסוק says: 'an elder, and you shall fear.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another part of the ברייתא. Now the focus turns to the elder's side: he should not make people stand for him without need.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now we spoke about the duty of others to honor the elder. Here רבי שמעון בן אלעזר reads the words 'זקן' and 'ויראת' next to each other as a message to the elder himself. He too should have fear of Heaven and not put a burden on people.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says:
From where is it known that an elder should not trouble others?
The verse says: "An elder, and you shall fear."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 19:32

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר: מִנַּיִן לְזָקֵן שֶׁלֹּא יַטְרִיחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the ברייתא and turns from the duty of others to the duty of the elder.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An elder should not trouble people to honor him.

steps.title: A scholar who walks around people lives long
steps.stepSummary: אביי says there is a tradition that a scholar who goes around so people will not need to stand will live long. אביי and רבי זירא did this.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: We have a tradition that if he goes around, he will live. אביי would go around, and רבי זירא would go around.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי adds a reward to רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's teaching. The גמרא then reports that אביי and רבי זירא both acted this way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A scholar who takes a longer path so people will not have to stand is not troubling them. אביי says this earns long life. The two rabbis' practice shows they took this seriously.

keyTerms.meaning: Goes around, takes a roundabout path

steps.whatToRemember: Others must honor the elder, but the elder himself should try not to burden them.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: נָקְטִינַן דְּאִי מַקֵּיף – חָיֵי.
phrases.english: Abaye said: We hold that if he goes around, he lives.
phrases.notes: He means going around the people so they won't have to stand up for him.

phrases.english: Abaye would go around; Rabbi Zeira would go around.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: נָקְטִינַן דְּאִי מַקֵּיף חָיֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a reward and real practice to the rule that an elder should not trouble people.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A scholar who goes around to spare people from standing will live long.

steps.title: רבינא complains about a man who did not cover his head
steps.stepSummary: A man passed in front of רבי ירמיה מדיפתי without covering his head, and רבינא called him rude.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא was sitting before רבי ירמיה מדיפתי. A man passed in front of him and did not cover his head. רבינא said: How rude this man is!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells another story about honoring a rabbi. רבינא objects that a man did not show respect to his teacher.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Covering one's head was a way of showing respect when passing a rabbi. רבינא sees the man skip this and calls it rudeness. This complaint sets up רבי ירמיה's answer in the next step.

phrases.english: Ravina was sitting before
Rabbi Yirmeya of Difti,
a certain man passed before him
and did not cover his head.
He said: How rude is this man.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר: כַּמָּה חֲצִיף הָא גַּבְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new story about showing honor to a rabbi.
steps.kashyaTarget: The man who passed without covering his head.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Passing a rabbi without a sign of respect looks like rudeness.

steps.title: He may come from a town full of rabbis
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה answers that the man may be from מתא מחסיא, where rabbis are common, so people there are less careful.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Perhaps he is from מתא מחסיא, where rabbis are common.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה defends the man. He suggests the man grew up where rabbis are everywhere, so he was not being rude on purpose.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a town full of rabbis, people get used to them and stop making a big show of honor. So the man's behavior may come from his local habit, not from a lack of respect. רבי ירמיה judges him kindly.

keyTerms.meaning: A town in Babylonia, home of a large yeshiva

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: דִּלְמָא מִמָּתָא מַחְסֵיָא נִיהוּ,
phrases.english: He said to him: Perhaps he is from Mata Mechasya,
where people are used to rabbis.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: דִּלְמָא מִמָּתָא מַחְסֵיָא נִיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבינא's complaint in step 25.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The man was being rude to the rabbi.
steps.terutzMaskana: He may come from a place where people are so used to rabbis that they are less careful.

steps.title: איסי בן יהודה: every elderly person deserves standing
steps.stepSummary: איסי בן יהודה reads 'מפני שיבה תקום' as including every elderly person, even one who is not a scholar.
steps.simpleTranslation: איסי בן יהודה says: 'Before the hoary head you shall stand' means that any elderly person is included.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new opinion. איסי בן יהודה says the פסוק about standing up applies to every old person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the פסוק was read as speaking about a זקן who is a Torah scholar. איסי בן יהודה reads the word שיבה (old age) on its own terms, so age alone is enough to earn this honor.

keyTerms.meaning: Old age, gray hair; an elderly person

phrases.english: Isi ben Yehuda says:
"Before the hoary head you shall stand"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 19:32

phrases.english: even any elderly person is included in the meaning.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיסִי בֶּן יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the stories about scholars back to who is included in the מצוה of standing.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Any elderly person, even one who is not learned, is included in 'מפני שיבה תקום'.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן rules like איסי בן יהודה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן gives the practical ruling: the הלכה follows איסי בן יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: The הלכה follows איסי בן יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן decides the practical law. We follow איסי בן יהודה, so we stand for any elderly person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This turns איסי בן יהודה's reading from just one opinion into the practical rule. The stories that come next show how this ruling was actually carried out.
steps.whyThisMatters: This ruling is why the מצוה of standing up applies to every elderly person, not only to Torah scholars.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
The halacha follows Isi ben Yehuda.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲלָכָה כְּאִיסִי בֶּן יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the practical ruling on איסי בן יהודה's view.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: We stand for every elderly person.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן stands for non-Jewish elders, while רבא only shows honor
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן stood even for non-Jewish elders because of everything they had lived through. רבא did not stand for them but still showed them respect.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן would stand before Aramean elders. He said: How many experiences have passed over these people! רבא would not actually stand for them, but he showed them honor.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells how רבי יוחנן carried out his own ruling. He stood even for non-Jewish elders, and רבא honored them in a lighter way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן's reason is the life experience that comes with old age, and that applies to non-Jews too. רבא agrees they deserve respect, but he shows it with a gesture of honor instead of fully standing up.

keyTerms.meaning: Experiences, things a person has gone through

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan would stand
before Aramean elders.
phrases.notes: "Aramean" here just means non-Jewish.

phrases.english: He said: How many experiences
have passed over these people!
Rava would not actually stand up,
but he showed them honor.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן הֲוָה קָאֵי מִקַּמֵּי סָבֵי דְאַרְמָאֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows רבי יוחנן's ruling in practice, stretched even to non-Jewish elders.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Non-Jewish elders also deserve respect. רבי יוחנן stood for them, and רבא showed them honor without standing.

steps.title: How אביי, רבא and רב נחמן helped elders
steps.stepSummary: אביי gave elders his own hand, רבא sent a messenger, and רב נחמן sent his servants, explaining that the honor of his Torah stopped him from doing it himself. Then a new teaching of רבי איבו in the name of רבי ינאי is introduced.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי would give his hand to elders. רבא would send his messenger. רב נחמן would send his servants. He said: If not for the Torah, how many people named נחמן בר אבא are there in the marketplace? רבי איבו said in the name of רבי ינאי:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא lists how three אמוראים helped elders, each in his own way. The last line starts a new teaching that continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All three helped elders. אביי did it with his own hand, while רבא and רב נחמן did it through others. רב נחמן explains that his importance comes only from Torah, so he must not lower that honor, and he still does the מצוה through his servants.

keyTerms.meaning: Gave a hand, to lean on

steps.confusionAlert: רב נחמן is not saying he is too proud to help. He means his honor belongs to the Torah, so he does the מצוה through his servants instead of personally.

phrases.english: Abaye would give his hand to elders.
Rava would send his messenger.
Rav Nachman would send his servants.
He said: If not for the Torah,

phrases.aramaic: כַּמָּה נַחְמָן בַּר אַבָּא אִיכָּא בְּשׁוּקָא?
phrases.english: how many Nachman bar Abbas are there in the marketplace?
phrases.notes: He means that without Torah he would be just another ordinary man, so he must protect the Torah's honor.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אַיְיבוּ אָמַר רַבִּי יַנַּאי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Aivu said in the name of Rabbi Yannai:

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבָּיֵי יָהֵיב יְדָא לְסָבֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the examples of how אמוראים honored elders, moving from standing to physically helping them.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Helping elders can be done personally or through others. A great scholar may use agents to protect the honor of his Torah.
